naive_small.description: Scaled Naive-style workload (3 columns, 3,000 rows, 4 query templates, recall@100 >= 0.90 per template, budget 3 indexes). Plans are scored on held-out query instances of each template. Paper-reported values are kept as transcribed earlier: 2.1x is the low end of the paper's HNSW/DiskANN speedup range (Fig. 7B/8B), i.e. normalized cost 0.48. For reference, Fig. 7 (HNSW) shows Naive latency speedup ~6.5x and normalized cost ~0.33 (Mint 0.44e7 vs PerColumn 1.34e7; PerQuery ~0.21 with 33% more storage). The scaled 3,000-row synthetic setup is not expected to match these magnitudes, only their direction.

weighted_cost.description: Probability-weighted mean query cost on held-out query instances (index-scan dim*ek plus re-rank query-dim*distinct candidates), normalized by the evaluator's fixed PerColumn plans on the same instances. Failed runs get a fixed worst value.

mean_recall_at_k.description: Mean over query templates of the template's mean recall@k on held-out instances.

min_recall_at_k.description: Worst template's mean recall@k on held-out instances; must be >= the 0.90 floor or the run is failed.

recall_floor_violation.description: Amount by which the worst template's mean recall falls below the floor (failed runs: the full floor).

storage_indexes.description: Number of distinct indexes with ek > 0 across all template plans, plus any further indexes in a declared configuration (a declaration can only add storage). Tie-breaker only: the paper treats storage as a constraint at a fixed budget.

storage_budget_violation.description: Indexes used beyond the storage budget; any violation fails the run.

mean_candidate_multiplier_at_k.description: Mean over templates of the mean distinct-candidate count divided by k. Tie-breaker only (already part of cost).

max_candidate_multiplier_at_k.description: Largest template mean distinct-candidate count divided by k. Tie-breaker only (unweighted by template probability).

speedup_vs_per_column.description: Evaluator-fixed PerColumn cost divided by the submission's cost on the same held-out instances (0 for failed runs).

bicomplex_small.description: Scaled BiComplex-style workload (5 columns, 3,000 rows, 8 query templates over column subsets with >= 2 columns, recall@100 >= 0.90 per template, budget 5 indexes = number of columns). Plans are scored on held-out query instances. Paper values (HNSW, read from Fig. 7; 8 columns, 12 queries, 1M rows, budget 8): Mint cost ~0.56e7 vs PerColumn ~1.71e7 (normalized ~0.33, cost ratio ~3.05x; latency speedup ~7.3x in Fig. 7B); PerQuery ~0.40e7 (normalized ~0.23) using 12 indexes. Storage values are the paper's (budget 8); this scaled setup uses a budget of 5.
